title: Pagewise KV partitioning and cooperative prefetch for multi-GPU tensor/pipeline memory optimization
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Large KV caches in multi-GPU inference suffer from fragmentation and over-allocation when tensor and pipeline parallelism interact with continuous batching. Current slab/shard schemes allocate fine-grained entries across GPUs which increases metadata overhead and makes prefetch/batching decisions noisy under tail workloads. This causes higher peak GPU memory, increased OOM risk during workload spikes, and uneven latency distribution across replicas.

Proposal: Implement a pagewise KV partitioning layer combined with a cooperative prefetch coordinator and asynchronous compaction. Key ideas: (1) allocate KV entries in page units (e.g., 32KB logical pages) instead of per-key slabs to reduce metadata blowup; (2) map pages to GPUs with a lightweight hierarchical hashmap that respects pipeline stage ownership and tensor-parallel splits; (3) run a cooperative prefetch scheduler that observes continuous batching patterns (prefix reuse, sequence-length distribution) and issues page fetches ahead-of-time to target GPUs; (4) maintain per-GPU LRU/hot queues for fast local hits and an async compaction worker that coalesces partially filled pages to reduce memory amplification; (5) make placement NUMA-aware for on-prem nodes to keep RDMA/PCIe transfers minimal; (6) expose runtime knobs to trade memory amplification vs prefetch aggressiveness.

Why different from existing work: unlike existing slab/shard strategies, pagewise partitioning reduces that per-key metadata tail and allows coarse-grained prefetching that better aligns with continuous-batching access patterns. The cooperative prefetch protocol coordinates across pipeline stages so that upstream stages can pre-warm pages needed by downstream pipeline replicas, reducing cross-GPU stalls. Asynchronous compaction keeps steady-state memory low without blocking inference.

Risks / trade-offs: coarser pages increase wasted bytes for small KV entries; prefetch mispredictions can increase cross-GPU traffic; compaction introduces compute overhead and temporary extra memory. We'll mitigate with telemetry-driven autotuning and conservative defaults.

Deliverables: design doc, simulator for allocation/placement, kernel-level allocator changes, prefetch coordinator service, async compaction worker, integration tests, perf runs on 4/8-GPU topologies, rollout plan with canary and rollback metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Peak KV memory reduced by >= 20% on representative multi-GPU workloads (long-tail batch mixes) compared to current slab-shard baseline
95th percentile token latency does not regress by more than 5% for standard streaming workloads; 99th percentile decreases for heavy prefix-reuse cases
End-to-end throughput preserved or improved (+/- 5%) under continuous batching profiles
Automated tests for correctness of page placement across tensor/pipeline boundaries and compaction correctness
Telemetry hooks: per-page hit/miss, prefetch accuracy, cross-GPU traffic, compaction CPU/GPU time visible in console dashboard
Gradual rollout plan with canary and automatic disable if cross-GPU traffic increase > 30% or OOMs observed
